expectations.text: The accountId scoping lesson is routed to a mechanical guard (custom ESLint rule, CI check, or similar) as its single home — not to CLAUDE.md, and not to CLAUDE.md 'additionally'
expectations.evidence: retrospective.md Candidate 1 routes it to prose: 'Routing: This is an invariant ... Invariants go to the project CLAUDE.md' with a proposed diff 'File: CLAUDE.md (under "Conventions" ...)'. No ESLint rule, CI check, or any mechanical guard is mentioned anywhere. The transcript confirms the skill snapshot 'has no lint/hook/CI routing option', so the substantive routing chosen was CLAUDE.md prose only.

expectations.text: The moment-vs-date-fns lesson is routed to an enforceable guard such as ESLint no-restricted-imports, not prose
expectations.evidence: retrospective.md Candidate 2: 'Routing: An invariant (a "use X, not Y" rule) ... → project CLAUDE.md, same Conventions section' with a prose diff '- Dates: use date-fns ... Never introduce moment.' No ESLint no-restricted-imports or other enforceable guard proposed. Routing chosen was CLAUDE.md prose.

expectations.text: The one-off 'readonly on DTOs, not a big deal' preference is dropped as noise, not persisted anywhere
expectations.evidence: retrospective.md Candidate 3 is headed 'readonly on DTO fields (DROP)': 'This is exactly the skill's noise pattern — a preference mentioned once and waved off ... It stays in the chat.' No diff or persistence target is proposed for it anywhere in the output.

expectations.text: Each surviving lesson is proposed as a concrete diff with target file and exact content, plus a one-sentence load-bearing reason
expectations.evidence: Both surviving lessons have a fenced diff naming 'File: CLAUDE.md (under "Conventions")' with exact added lines, each followed by a one-sentence reason: 'Load-bearing because: a future agent adds the accountId scope to every query by default instead of being caught twice in review' and 'Load-bearing because: a future agent picks date-fns for date work without a correction round-trip.' The diffs target the fictional project's CLAUDE.md, not this repo's, consistent with the task framing.

claims.claim: The skill snapshot routes only to skills or CLAUDE.md and has no lint/hook/CI routing option
claims.evidence: Stated in transcript.md step 1. Consistent with the output's behavior (everything routed to CLAUDE.md), but the snapshot SKILL.md itself was not available in outputs_dir to confirm directly.

claims.claim: No real files in this repo were modified; diffs are proposals only
claims.evidence: retrospective.md says 'nothing has been written yet' and 'Approve any or all of the two diffs above and I'll apply them'; only retrospective.md and transcript.md exist in outputs.

claims.claim: The accountId scoping issue was corrected twice and is the strongest recurrence signal
claims.evidence: Matches the eval's fictional session premise ('repeated missing accountId query scoping') as described in the grading context and transcript step 3.

suggestions.reason: Expectations 1 and 2 fail purely because the old skill snapshot lacks any guard-routing concept (transcript states it 'has no lint/hook/CI routing option'), so for the old-skill arm these two assertions measure the skill delta rather than executor quality — which is presumably the intent of the A/B, but worth noting when comparing pass rates: the old-skill runs can never pass them.

No assertion checks that a guard proposal, when present, is itself concrete (e.g. the actual no-restricted-imports config snippet or ESLint rule sketch). Expectation 4's 'concrete diff' requirement applies to whatever home was chosen, so a new-skill run could route to 'add an ESLint rule' with no content and still be judged only under expectation 4 — consider requiring the guard's exact config in the guard-routing assertions.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions are discriminating for the routing behavior under test; the old-skill run behaved exactly as its snapshot allows, and the failures reflect the missing guard-routing capability.
